provenance.notes: Production code (data/ecmwf.py, scripts/pilot_phase7_ecmwf.py including its launch driver) was fully committed at commit c95b54d BEFORE extraction began -- no uncommitted fixes were required during or after the run. The entire 904-item dataset is reproducible from this single commit. Production output used its own dedicated directory (data/processed/pilot/ecmwf/), never shared with any validation/benchmark script (all prior ECMWF validation/benchmark work ran from Claude's scratchpad directory, outside the repo) -- confirmed via a pre-launch check that the directory did not yet exist, and post-run reconciliation confirming the checkpoint's 904 keys match the independently-recomputed canonical work-item set exactly (0 missing, 0 extra). 0 extraction failures occurred during the run (0 retries needed) -- data/ecmwf.py's internal backoff/retry logic, built for this bucket's known aggressive rate-limiting, was never required to intervene.

source.name: ecmwf_deterministic
source.fh0_semantics: 2t/2d/10u/10v/sp present and meaningful at F0. tp is present but degenerate (zero-width window, value=0.0) -- explicitly skipped. mx2t3/mn2t3 at F0 are degenerate placeholders decoding to 0.0 Kelvin (physically impossible) -- explicitly skipped. 0 rows for tp/ssrd/mx2t3/mn2t3/mx2t6/mn2t6 confirmed at forecast_hour=0 in the final dataset.
source.window_semantics: tp/ssrd are pure cumulative-since-run-start at every forecast hour (never differenced in this extraction). mx2t3/mn2t3 (rolling 3h window) apply for forecast_hour<=144; mx2t6/mn2t6 (rolling 6h window) apply for forecast_hour>144 -- a real regime switch caught during validation and explicitly handled, not silently missed. This 40-day production run's target-day-only design never required forecast hours beyond F39, so mx2t6/mn2t6 do not appear in this dataset (0 rows) -- not a defect, a consequence of the lead-in extraction window never reaching the 6-hourly regime.
source.availability_finding: All forecast hours of a run share Last-Modified within a 37-59 second window at a typical ~514-minute lag from run_time -- confirmed a bulk archive-sync event, not genuine per-forecast-hour progressive dissemination. Production-scale audit found 2 of 144 runs (2025-02-24 12Z and 2025-02-25 00Z, both real selected-pilot-day runs) with anomalously longer lag (718 and 1436 minutes respectively) while still maintaining full internal atomicity (all variables of each affected run shared the same lag) -- a genuine, occasional archive-sync delay, not a data-quality defect. See docs/ecmwf_pilot_readiness.md and manifest 'performance' section.

runtime_overrides.note: matches scripts/pilot_phase7_ecmwf.py's own committed default (independently benchmarked for ECMWF, see docs/ecmwf_pilot_readiness.md sections 30-31) -- no override needed

actual_availability_lag_minutes.note: Extremely tight P10-P90 band (0.08 min) confirms the near-atomic bulk-sync finding at full production scale. The max (1436 min) reflects 2 of 144 runs with a genuine, occasional archive-sync delay (still internally atomic within each affected run) -- not a data-quality defect.

performance.estimate_vs_actual_note: Pre-launch estimates (docs/ecmwf_pilot_readiness.md sections 34-36, from a 12-item benchmark sample) were ~5.6 GB remote / ~0.8 MB local / (runtime not separately estimated, benchmark showed high variance). Actual full-scale production run: ~5.99 GB remote (close match), ~0.76 MB local (close match), 14.15 minutes runtime at 1.065 items/sec sustained throughput -- faster than every individual benchmark trial (0.37-0.94 items/sec), consistent with the pattern observed in every other pilot in this project (a sustained long run outperforms short repeated-trial benchmarks). 0 retries were needed, better than anticipated given this bucket's known rate-limiting behavior.
